Hey all — looping in the implementation details so Nimbus and AWS have what they need. Below is a concise mapping and a couple of operational notes.

1) SKU -> dimension mapping (proposal)
"nimbus-basic" -> dimension: concurrent_sessions
"nimbus-pro" -> dimension: api_calls
"nimbus-enterprise" -> dimension: active_users

2) Payload / UsageRecord cadence - We aggregate at 1-hour windows and send UsageRecord with: {timestamp, dimensionName, quantity, customerIdentifier}. If Nimbus prefers daily aggregates we can switch to 24h windows; the platform supports both.

3) Entitlement handling - Preferred pattern: AWS Marketplace sends an entitlement webhook to Redwood with the AWS account id and product code; Redwood creates a linked entitlement record. For edge cases where webhooks are delayed, Redwood runs a daily reconciliation job against the Marketplace entitlement API to ensure no drift. Seat revocation is executed via an entitlement state change (ACTIVE->REVOKED) and we emit an audit event + optional user deprovisioning webhook to Nimbus.

4) Failure modes and retries - UsageRecord sends are idempotent (we include an idempotency token per hour window). If AWS Metering API returns 5xx, we backoff and retry; if records fail for >24h we alert the on-call and create a HubSpot ticket (see link).

5) Example curl (UsageRecord):
curl -X POST https://metering.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/2016-10-01/put-usage-records 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"ProductCode":"NIMBUS-PRO","UsageRecords":[{"Timestamp":"2026-08-17T10:00:00Z","CustomerIdentifier":"aws-cust-1234","Dimension":"api_calls","Quantity":152}]}'

Hi Procurement Team — welcome, and thanks for the contract. Short answers:

- Yes: Redwood maps Marketplace cancellations to entitlement revocation. We support immediate and delayed (end-of-term) revocation policies; we can implement the policy you prefer.
- SLA: our target for UsageRecord delivery to AWS is within 15 minutes for streaming paths and <1 hour for batched hourly pushes. We publish per-route latency metrics in the Redwood Console and can include a clause in the SOW for the pilot.

Onboarding milestones (proposed):
1) Contract countersign (DocuSign) — Day 0
2) SKU mapping + entitlement test (3 business days)
3) Small pilot (5 customers, 1 week)
4) Production enablement and co-sell listing (go/no-go review)
